method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

supports: x-pharmacology-029: renal impairment increases digoxin accumulation/toxicity
x-pharmacology-031: sildenafil potentiates nitrate hypotension; concurrent use contraindicated
sourceChecks.scope: Specific interaction support; no numeric interval asserted.

supports: x-pharmacology-037: timing, platelet decline, thrombosis and cessation of heparin when HIT suspected
sourceChecks.scope: Specific recognition/escalation support; does not authorize independent LPN prescribing.

items.assessment: Tongue swelling/voice change during ACE therapy is an airway emergency even without rash; emergency assessment is defensible.
New dry cough temporally linked to ACE therapy with no congestion/infection cues supports medication review rather than independent cessation.
Key is defensible, but avoiding all fruits/vegetables and recommending salt only on dosing days are weak distractors.
issues: Key is defensible, but avoiding all fruits/vegetables and recommending salt only on dosing days are weak distractors.
proposedChanges: Replace option 2 with: Separate the salt substitute from spironolactone by two hours. Replace option 3 with: Start it now and review potassium at the usual annual visit. Explain that dose separation does not remove potassium retention and monitoring/review should precede routine use.

items.assessment: Pulse48, new GI/visual symptoms and renal decline support withholding pending urgent toxicity/rhythm review; old therapeutic level does not reassure.
Muscle pain/weakness plus dark urine warrants urgent muscle/renal injury review; lipid testing and food timing do not address the acute concern.
Recent sildenafil contraindicates nitrate despite current normal pressure; chest pain still requires urgent alternative assessment.
Improved edema with stable standing pressure and less exertional dyspnea support benefit; hypotension, hypokalemia or worsening oxygen need do not.
Confusion with sodium124 during thiazide therapy merits withholding pending urgent assessment; additional free water can worsen the problem.
Avoiding abrupt withdrawal and arranging a prescribed change is appropriate for controlled angina; symptom absence may reflect benefit.
Safe positioning/review keys are sound; brisk walking during lightheadedness is implausibly unsafe filler.
issues: Safe positioning/review keys are sound; brisk walking during lightheadedness is implausibly unsafe filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option 3 with: Give a large glass of water and repeat standing immediately without reviewing fluid restrictions. Explain that a fluid intervention requires context and does not replace initial safe positioning/reassessment.

items.assessment: Late dosing with nocturia supports earlier timing through the treatment plan; arbitrary dose/frequency change or fluid restriction is unjustified.

Day6 platelet drop over50% with possible thrombosis supports suspected HIT, stopping exposure under protocol and urgent escalation. Source supports cessation without waiting for labs when suspicion is intermediate/high.
Head impact during apixaban warrants urgent assessment despite normal initial exam; INR cannot establish absent anticoagulant effect.
Melena with dizziness and no iron/bismuth exposure supports circulation assessment and urgent GI bleeding escalation; screening pathways are insufficient.
Drug/procedure/renal function must inform an authorized perioperative plan; a generic schedule or normal INR is insufficient.
Gentle oral care and review of NSAIDs reduce avoidable bleeding; missed-dose advice is appropriately drug-specific rather than universal doubling.
Apixaban still requires clinical/renal/interaction review despite no routine INR titration; correct key distinguishes monitoring purpose.
Urgent circulation support is sound, but walking a client with BP78/44 and faintness is cartoonishly unsafe.
issues: Urgent circulation support is sound, but walking a client with BP78/44 and faintness is cartoonishly unsafe.
proposedChanges: Replace option 1 with: Repeat the blood pressure using the other arm before calling for help. Explain that rapid confirmation can accompany but should not delay response to symptomatic severe hypotension.

items.assessment: Residual edema does not exclude intravascular depletion; weight loss plus dry mouth and postural dizziness supports reassessment for overdiuresis.
Edema after amlodipine increase without weight/pulmonary/function change supports drug-effect review, avoiding automatic HF escalation.
Holding due rate-slowing doses pending urgent review is defensible; walking to increase pulse is an implausible response to near-syncope.
issues: Holding due rate-slowing doses pending urgent review is defensible; walking to increase pulse is an implausible response to near-syncope.
proposedChanges: Replace option 1 with: Give metoprolol alone because diltiazem was added more recently. Explain that both slow rate and an arbitrary choice does not resolve symptomatic bradycardia.

items.assessment: Renal/potassium trends plus BP/postural symptoms are appropriate, but INR without anticoagulation is irrelevant filler.
issues: Renal/potassium trends plus BP/postural symptoms are appropriate, but INR without anticoagulation is irrelevant filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option 2 with: Repeat only serum sodium because a diuretic is prescribed. Explain that sodium alone misses ACE-related potassium/renal changes and hemodynamic effects.

items.assessment: Prescribed nitrate-free interval limits tolerance; it does not remove the need for acute symptom action or authorize extra exposure.
Unexplained warfarin/DOAC overlap needs clarification before uncertain administration; arbitrary prolonged holds also create risk.
Schedule intervention is correct; doubling every missed workday dose is an implausibly blunt adherence fix.
issues: Schedule intervention is correct; doubling every missed workday dose is an implausibly blunt adherence fix.
proposedChanges: Replace option 1 with: Add a reminder alarm at the same clock time each day without discussing the rotating shifts. Explain that a fixed reminder alone may not make the prescribed schedule feasible.
